metaTitle: MMSU Tomato Hybrid 1: Yield, Maturity and Characteristics
metaDescription: MMSU Tomato Hybrid 1 is a tomato variety for Luzon, the Visayas and Mindanao. About 93 days to harvest, 30.8 t/ha in trials. See its ratings and traits.
excerpt: MMSU Tomato Hybrid 1 is a registered tomato variety. It was registered with the National Seed Industry Council in 2004 as NSIC 2004 Tm 10. MMSU Batac, Ilocos Norte bred it. It takes about 93 days from transplanting to the first harvest, with 30.84 tonnes per hectare on average in the trials.

blocks.text: How long does it take, and how much does it yield?

MMSU Tomato Hybrid 1 takes about 93 days from transplanting to the first harvest. That is 22.4 days longer than the average of the 20 tomato varieties with a day count, 70.6 days. A shorter crop frees the field sooner and dodges more of the weather, while a longer one often fills more.

Its average yield of 30.84 t/ha beats the average of its group, 20.91. It sits in the top quarter of its group. Trial yields come from well managed plots, so your own will depend on water, fertilizer, pests and timing.

Once you know the day count, anee.io dates every task from each lot's own planting day, with [the growth stages and weather](/features/growth-stages-and-weather) beside it.

blocks.text: It showed no weak spot in the ratings on record. Still, a resistant variety can break down when a new strain or pest population comes, so keep scouting. Read up on [leafminer](/pests/leafminer), [Fusarium wilt](/diseases/fusarium-wilt), [bacterial wilt](/diseases/bacterial-wilt).

The pests and diseases that hit tomato fields most often: [early blight](/diseases/early-blight), [late blight](/diseases/late-blight), [tomato leaf curl](/diseases/tomato-leaf-curl), [whitefly](/pests/whitefly), [anthracnose](/diseases/anthracnose). Our [pest finder](/pests) and [disease finder](/diseases) help you name what you see.
A fruit weighs about 31.04 grams. It is round.
Where and when to plant MMSU Tomato Hybrid 1

It is recommended for Luzon, the Visayas and Mindanao in the wet season. Bacterial wilt kills more lowland tomato than any other disease, so in the wet season pick a variety rated resistant to it. Choose a firm, oblong fruit if you sell to a far market, and a round, juicy one for fresh sale nearby. Heat tolerant hybrids set fruit in the hot months, when open pollinated tomatoes often drop their flowers. Before planting, get the field ready with our guide: [Land preparation for vegetables](/land-preparation/vegetable-land-preparation).
